hero.headline: Judge orders Trump's name removed from Kennedy Center
hero.body:
A federal judge has ordered the removal of Donald Trump's name from the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, ruling that the prestigious Washington D.C. venue cannot be renamed without congressional action.

U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper directed the Trump administration to remove all physical signage bearing Trump's name and eliminate any references to a "Trump Kennedy Center" from official materials within 14 days. In his 94-page opinion, Cooper wrote that the Kennedy Center's federal statute makes clear the institution is named for President John F. Kennedy and cannot bear any other formal name without congressional approval.

"Congress gave the Kennedy Center its name, and only Congress can change it," Cooper stated. He found that the Kennedy Center's board overstepped its authority when it voted to rename the facility after Trump.

The ruling also temporarily blocked the center from closing this summer for proposed renovations. Trump had announced a two-year closure to allow for extensive upgrades. Cooper criticized the board's decision to support the closure, saying it was based on insufficient information and neglected the center's statutory obligations and potential negative impacts on programming and memorial functions. He described the decision as "ill-informed and seemingly preordained."

The lawsuit was brought by Joyce Beatty, an Ohio Democratic U.S. representative who serves on the Kennedy Center's board by virtue of her congressional position. Beatty welcomed the ruling, stating that the decision "rightly affirms that this administration's efforts to rename and close the Center have no basis in law." She added that the Kennedy Center belongs to the American people, not to Trump.

Trump responded by posting on his Truth Social platform that he would work with Congress on transferring ownership of the Kennedy Center to them. He stated he had instructed the Department of Commerce to make arrangements with Congress for a complete transfer of the institution. Trump said he has no interest in continuing with the Kennedy Center "unless I am free to do what I do better than anyone else, bring this Institution back, physically, financially, and artistically."

Trump appointed himself chair of the Kennedy Center's board in February after taking office, calling it a "take-over." He purged the existing board and replaced its members with his own appointees. The reconstituted board voted in December to add Trump's name to the facility.

The renaming effort sparked significant backlash. Artists and performing groups canceled bookings in protest, including the Tony award-winning musical Hamilton. The National Symphony Orchestra's executive director left to take a position elsewhere. Richard Grenell, a Trump appointee who played a key role in pushing to overhaul the institution, stepped down as president in March.

The Kennedy Center is a federally-funded venue that has long enjoyed bipartisan support as one of America's leading arts institutions.

cards.headline: Americans Injured in Iranian Missile Strike on Kuwaiti Air Base
cards.body:
American military personnel were injured when Iranian missiles struck an air base in Kuwait, according to U.S. Central Command. The attack represents what U.S. officials described as a violation of a fragile ceasefire between the two nations.

The missile strike targeted the Kuwaiti air base where American forces are stationed. U.S. Central Command confirmed the attack and the injuries to American personnel in a press release, though specific numbers of wounded were not disclosed in the available reports.

U.S. officials characterized the Iranian attack as an egregious ceasefire violation. The strike occurred during a particularly sensitive period, as the incident came amid ongoing negotiations between Washington and Tehran. U.S. officials had previously confirmed that the two countries had agreed on a framework for a potential deal.

The timing of the attack has raised questions about the stability of any diplomatic progress. President Trump had scheduled a meeting with his advisers to make what he termed a final determination on Iran policy. That meeting took place without any deal being announced following the discussions.

The framework agreement between the United States and Iran had reportedly included provisions for pausing hostilities for a two-month period. The missile strike on the Kuwaiti base appears to have tested the limits of that understanding, according to reports describing the incident as a challenge to the fragile truce.

Kuwait hosts American military forces as part of U.S. operations in the Middle East region. The air base serves as one of several installations where U.S. personnel are deployed across the Gulf states. The attack marks a direct strike on infrastructure housing American troops in a country that is not directly party to U.S.-Iran tensions.

The Iranian missile launch comes at a time when the broader Middle East region faces multiple security challenges. The attack adds another layer of complexity to already tense relations between Washington and Tehran, and raises questions about the viability of diplomatic efforts to reduce tensions between the two countries.

cards.headline: Germany Deploys Troops to Lithuania to Deter Russian Aggression
cards.teaser: German forces have been stationed in Lithuania, a Baltic nation once occupied by Germany, to protect against potential Russian threats.
cards.body:
Germany has stationed military forces in Lithuania to help defend the Baltic nation against potential Russian threats. This deployment marks a historic reversal for Lithuania, which endured German occupation during World War II. This time, Lithuanian officials have welcomed the German soldiers.

The move reflects broader NATO concerns about Russian military activity in Eastern Europe. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte has emphasized the alliance's commitment to defending member states, stating the bloc stands "ready to defend every inch" of allied territory following recent Russian drone strikes in the region.

cards.headline: Colombia Holds Presidential Election Between Leftist Leader and Far-Right Challenger
cards.teaser: Colombian voters head to the polls as a leftist candidate leads but faces a surging far-right rival who calls himself The Tiger.
cards.body:
Colombia's presidential election is set for Sunday, featuring a contest between left and right with starkly different approaches to the country's decades-long armed conflict. The vote takes place against a backdrop of resurgent political violence.

The election highlights deep divisions over how to address Colombia's long-running struggles involving the army, paramilitaries, and armed dissidents. Recent weeks have seen violence affecting journalists and activists covering the conflict, underscoring the volatile climate surrounding the electoral process.

cards.headline: Ebola Outbreak Prompts Uganda to Close Border with Democratic Republic of Congo
cards.teaser: Uganda shut its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo as cases of a rare Ebola virus strain continue to rise.
cards.body:
Uganda has closed its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo following an outbreak of Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus strain. The rare form of Ebola is spreading in the eastern DRC's Ituri province, and Uganda has reported seven confirmed cases.

The WHO chief has traveled to the DRC to assess response efforts and called for an immediate ceasefire in eastern Congo, warning of a "catastrophic collision of disease and conflict" as the outbreak outpaces containment measures in an active conflict zone.

cards.headline: Space Force awards SpaceX $4.16 billion contract for missile-tracking satellites
cards.teaser: The U.S. Space Force contracted SpaceX to build a network of satellites designed to track airborne targets and missiles.
cards.body:
SpaceX has been awarded a $4.16 billion contract by the U.S. Space Force to develop missile-tracking satellites. The sensor-equipped satellites will enable the military to detect and track airborne targets from space as part of the Space Based Airborne Target Indicator Program.

The satellite constellation is linked to President Donald Trump's "Golden Dome" defense system initiative. This contract represents a significant portion of SpaceX's government work, which already accounted for one-fifth of the company's 2025 revenue according to its recent IPO filing.

cards.headline: DNA test could help millions with breast cancer avoid chemotherapy
cards.teaser: An international trial suggests a new screening method could identify patients who can safely skip chemotherapy treatment.
cards.body:
A new genomic test could spare millions of breast cancer patients from chemotherapy, according to results from an international trial. The test determines whether patients actually need the treatment based on their genetic profile, potentially transforming how the disease is treated worldwide.

Patients with low test scores could be treated with hormone therapy alone and achieve near-identical outcomes to those receiving chemotherapy. This personalized approach would allow many patients currently undergoing chemotherapy to avoid the treatment and its associated side effects when it would not provide significant benefit.

cards.headline: Russian Drone Strikes Romanian Territory, Injuring Civilians
cards.teaser: A Russian drone struck Romania near the Ukrainian border, marking the first attack to injure civilians in the NATO member country.
cards.body:
A Russian drone struck an apartment building in eastern Romania during an overnight attack on Ukraine, injuring two people and starting a fire. The incident marked the first time a drone from the conflict has caused civilian casualties on Romanian territory.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte responded by affirming the alliance's readiness to defend all member states. "Russia's reckless behaviour is a danger to us all," Rutte stated after speaking with Romanian President Nicuşor Dan. The strike has intensified concerns about NATO's ability to protect its territory from spillover effects of the Ukraine war and raised questions about alliance solidarity and Western commitment to collective defense.

cards.headline: Muslims Mark Eid al-Adha Across Middle East Amid Ongoing Conflicts
cards.teaser: Eid al-Adha celebrations were subdued across the Middle East as war continues and shortages of food and fuel affect the region.
cards.body:
Muslims across the Middle East observed Eid al-Adha with muted celebrations as conflicts persist throughout the region. From Iran to Gaza, the holiday was marked against a backdrop of ongoing warfare that has affected daily life across multiple countries.

Food and fuel shortages have compounded the impact of the conflicts on populations throughout the region. The combination of war and resource scarcity has diminished the traditional festivities associated with the Islamic holiday in affected areas.

cards.headline: Japan Tightens Immigration Rules, Forcing Some Foreign Business Owners to Leave
cards.teaser: New visa requirements under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi are compelling foreign business owners, including curry shop operators, to leave Japan.
cards.body:
Japan has implemented stricter immigration rules that are forcing some foreign business owners to leave the country, despite having established roots there. The new visa requirements have particularly affected operators of curry shops and other small businesses run by foreign nationals.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's government introduced the tightened visa rules as part of an immigration crackdown. Foreign business owners who have built lives and enterprises in Japan now face the prospect of having to depart due to the new restrictions.

cards.headline: Judge reopens Trump lawsuit demanding $10 billion from IRS
cards.teaser: A judge ordered Trump to address allegations about whether a settlement creating a $1.8 billion fund constituted fraud.
cards.body:
A federal judge has reopened Trump's lawsuit against the IRS, ordering the president to respond to questions about a settlement agreement that established a $1.8 billion fund. The judge is investigating whether the deal constitutes fraud, characterizing the allegations as serious enough to require further examination.

Trump is seeking $10 billion from the IRS through the lawsuit. The court's focus centers on determining the legitimacy of the settlement that created the fund in question.

cards.headline: Trump in excellent health after annual physical, White House says
cards.teaser: The president's doctor says Trump is fully fit to carry out his duties despite some minor health observations.
cards.body:
The White House released results from President Trump's latest annual medical examination, stating he is "fully fit" to carry out his presidential duties.

The physician's report noted some findings including leg swelling and hand bruising, along with a recommendation that Trump lose weight and exercise more. Despite these observations, the doctor characterized his overall health status as strong and suitable for the demands of the presidency.

cards.headline: Paxton attacks opponent's masculinity in Texas Senate race
cards.teaser: The Republican Senate nominee called his Democratic opponent 'too low-T for Texas' after winning the primary runoff.
cards.body:
Ken Paxton attacked Democratic state Representative James Talarico shortly after winning the Texas Republican Senate primary runoff, calling him "too low-T for Texas." The comment brought questions about masculinity to the forefront of the general election campaign.

Talarico will face Paxton in the November general election as the Democratic nominee. Paxton's attack has made what it means to be a man a central theme of the race.

cards.headline: Lawmakers criticize closed primaries as limiting voter choice
cards.teaser: Some members of Congress say single-party primary elections incentivize party loyalty over broader representation.
cards.body:
Some lawmakers are speaking out against closed, single-party primary elections, arguing they limit voter choice and push elected officials toward party loyalty. The criticism focuses on how the primary system shapes behavior in Congress.

The lawmakers say the closed primary structure creates incentives for members of Congress to prioritize their party base over broader constituencies. They view single-party primaries as part of a system that restricts participation and narrows the range of acceptable political positions.

cards.headline: Four more rescued from flooded Laos cave after 10 days
cards.teaser: Two of seven villagers who entered the tunnels searching for gold on May 20 remain missing.
cards.body:
Rescue teams have freed four more men from a flooded cave system in Laos, following the successful extraction of one man earlier in the operation. The seven villagers entered the narrow tunnels on May 20 while searching for gold. Four of the remaining men were found huddled together on a rocky ledge approximately 300 metres from the cave entrance.

Two villagers remain missing as divers continue navigating the treacherous flooded passages. The rescue operation requires teams to crawl through narrow, water-filled tunnels while avoiding sharp rocks and potential collapse hazards.

hero.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes on launchpad during test in Florida
hero.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on the launchpad at Cape Canaveral in Florida during a scheduled test, threatening NASA's plans to build a lunar base and return humans to the moon within the next two years.

The explosion occurred at Launch Complex 36 during a "hotfire" test at 9 p.m. ET on Thursday. A massive fireball engulfed and destroyed the launchpad seconds after the test began. The blast was visible across Florida's space coast, with an orange sky seen as far south as Fort Pierce, 115 miles away. Shockwaves were felt in nearby communities, and residents in South Carolina hundreds of miles north reported seeing a glow in the sky.

Blue Origin founder Jeff Bezos confirmed that all company employees were safe and uninjured. The company described the incident as "an anomaly" but has not yet released details about the cause or the extent of damage to the launch complex.

The New Glenn rocket is critical to Blue Origin's space ambitions. The company had just won a NASA contract on Tuesday to launch the first of three planned missions this year to begin construction of a $20 billion lunar base. Blue Origin is also competing with SpaceX to provide a lunar lander for the Artemis IV mission scheduled for 2028, which will mark humanity's first return to the moon since 1972.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said the agency would conduct a full evaluation of the timeline's impact following the explosion. "Spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult," he stated, adding that NASA would work with its partners to investigate the incident and assess impacts to the Artemis and Moon Base programs.

Bezos acknowledged the setback in a social media post, saying "It's too early to know the root cause but we're already working to find it." He added, "Very rough day, but we'll rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying. It's worth it."

The explosion represents another challenge for Blue Origin as it attempts to compete with SpaceX. The company has faced recent setbacks, including a payload that ended up in the wrong orbit during a flight last month, resulting in a temporary FAA grounding. Thursday's test was the first static fire test since the FAA cleared the rocket to return to flight the previous week.

Elon Musk, whose SpaceX has dominated the commercial space industry, responded to the explosion on social media, stating simply that rockets are difficult. Both companies have constructed major facilities near Cape Canaveral to support NASA's Artemis program, which aims to land astronauts on the lunar surface in the coming years.

cards.teaser: Dell shares soared to an all-time high after the company reported strong quarterly results fueled by artificial intelligence server sales.

Since the source material doesn't confirm the facts in your original card, I'm returning it unchanged:

Original card text:

Dell stock jumped to a new record following a quarterly earnings report that exceeded expectations. The surge was driven by increased demand for AI servers, reflecting the ongoing boom in artificial intelligence infrastructure spending.

The stock's rise added $34 billion to founder Michael Dell's personal fortune, making him wealthier than Mark Zuckerberg. The company's outlook, boosted by AI server demand, prompted analysts to raise their assessments. The strong quarter set up what one market commentator called a crucial week for AI-related stocks.

cards.headline: Replimune gets third attempt at FDA approval after agency leadership change
cards.teaser: The biotech company will resubmit its cancer drug application following talks with the FDA after a leadership transition at the agency.
cards.body:
Replimune announced it will resubmit its cancer drug for FDA approval after productive discussions with the agency. The drug had been rejected twice before, but the company is making a third attempt following changes at the FDA, including the departure of a senior official.

The company's stock jumped 80 percent on the news. Replimune held talks with the FDA that the company characterized as productive, leading to the decision to prepare a new submission. The resubmission follows a shakeup in FDA leadership.

cards.headline: Southwest revises extra-seat policy for larger passengers after backlash
cards.teaser: The airline changed its seating rules for passengers who require additional space following four months of criticism.
cards.body:
Southwest Airlines updated its policy regarding passengers who need extra seats. The change comes after the airline faced backlash for four months over its previous approach to seating passengers of size.

The airline had implemented a seating rule that generated controversy among customers and advocacy groups. Southwest has now rolled back elements of that policy, though the company has not detailed all the specific changes to how it handles requests for additional seats.

cards.headline: China expands digital yuan use to lottery draws and government spending
cards.teaser: China is broadening the applications of its central bank digital currency beyond consumer transactions.
cards.body:
China has expanded the use of its digital yuan to include lottery systems and fiscal spending by government entities. The move represents a significant widening of the digital currency's footprint beyond its initial consumer-focused applications.

The digital yuan rollout comes as China positions itself in the global digital currency landscape. Some analysts suggest China is prepared to counter efforts by other nations, including potential digital dollar initiatives, that might compete for international capital flows and savings.

cards.headline: Exxon Mobil oil inventories rise as Iran conflict disrupts trade
cards.teaser: The energy company is accumulating unusually high levels of oil inventory due to trade disruptions linked to conflict with Iran.
cards.body:
Exxon Mobil is approaching record inventory levels as ongoing conflict involving Iran blocks normal oil trade routes. The buildup represents an unusual accumulation for the energy giant.

The Iran conflict has created obstacles for oil shipments and trade, forcing companies to adjust their logistics and storage strategies. Exxon's inventory situation reflects broader disruptions in global energy markets caused by the military situation.

hero.headline: Proposed federal rule would allow cancellation of research grants at any time
hero.body:
The federal government has proposed new funding rules that would permit the cancellation of research grants at any time without standard protections. The proposed changes would also make peer review optional for grant awards.

Under the proposed rules, political staff would screen grant applications for forbidden topics before funding decisions. The changes represent a shift from traditional research funding procedures that have relied on peer review and competitive evaluation processes.

The new framework would give federal agencies broad authority to terminate grants that have already been awarded. Researchers would no longer have the same assurances that approved projects would continue through their planned duration.

The proposal includes provisions allowing political appointees to review research topics before grants proceed. This screening process would apply to applications that have already undergone scientific evaluation.

Peer review has traditionally served as the foundation of federal research funding, with scientific experts evaluating proposals for merit and feasibility. The optional nature of peer review under the proposed rules would eliminate this requirement for some grant programs.

Federal research grants typically fund work at universities, research institutions, and laboratories across the country. These grants support projects ranging from basic science to applied research in fields including medicine, engineering, and environmental science.

The ability to cancel grants at any time could affect ongoing research projects that depend on multi-year funding commitments. Many scientific studies require sustained support to produce meaningful results.

The proposed rules apply to federal funding mechanisms used by agencies that support scientific research. Implementation would require final approval after a regulatory review process.

Researchers often plan projects based on the expectation that approved grants will continue barring misconduct or failure to meet stated objectives. The proposed changes would expand the circumstances under which funding could be withdrawn.

The screening process for forbidden topics would add a political review layer to grant decisions. The specific topics that would trigger scrutiny have not been publicly detailed in the proposal.

cards.headline: Space Force awards SpaceX $6.45 billion in contracts
cards.teaser: The contracts come ahead of SpaceX's planned initial public offering.
cards.body:
The Space Force has awarded SpaceX $6.45 billion in contracts as the company moves toward going public. The contracts mark an expansion of SpaceX's existing work with the military space branch.

Government contracts have become increasingly important to SpaceX's business. According to the company's IPO filing, one-fifth of its 2025 revenue came from government contracts, underscoring the significant role these partnerships play in the company's overall operations.

cards.headline: DuckDuckGo search traffic increases following Google's AI integration
cards.teaser: Users are turning to the privacy-focused search engine as Google expands AI features.
cards.body:
DuckDuckGo has experienced a surge in installations and usage following Google's announcement of expanded AI integration into its search product at its annual developer conference. The privacy-focused search engine positions itself as an alternative for users concerned about AI's role in search results.

The timing of DuckDuckGo's traffic increase coincides with growing user interest in search options that differ from Google's AI-enhanced approach, according to reports from MacRumors and PCMag.

cards.headline: Court blocks US plan to relocate Ebola-exposed Americans to Kenya
cards.teaser: A Kenyan court has stopped the Trump administration from transferring exposed individuals to the country.
cards.body:
A Kenyan court has blocked the Trump administration's plan to build a quarantine and treatment center in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola during an outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

The White House had confirmed it was setting up the facility in Kenya as an alternative to bringing exposed Americans back to the United States for quarantine. Some experts have criticized this approach, arguing that preventing Americans from returning home could hinder treatment efforts. The United States has previously constructed specialized facilities designed for handling individuals exposed to infectious diseases.

cards.headline: Nvidia and Microsoft tease laptop processor announcement
cards.teaser: The companies have posted coordinated messages about what may be new N1X processors.
cards.body:
Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm are teasing an upcoming announcement with coordinated social media posts. Both the Windows and Nvidia GeForce accounts posted "A new era of PC" on X, with Arm following suit.

The companies are expected to announce Nvidia's new N1X laptop processors at Computex this weekend. Microsoft also teased new Surface hardware, with Surface chief Pavan Davuluri posting a mysterious image of what appears to be a curved display edge and hinting that "something new is coming for developers."

cards.headline: Researchers warn AI coding tools may compromise code quality
cards.teaser: While AI helps programmers write code faster, the resulting code may not be better.
cards.body:
Some programmers are now refusing to work without AI coding assistance, according to researchers studying the trend. The tools help developers produce code more quickly than traditional methods.

Researchers have issued a warning that AI-assisted coding may not produce better quality code despite the speed improvements. The researchers caution that reliance on these tools could create problems in software development over time.

cards.headline: Indian court ruling on Google ad business draws criticism from founders
cards.teaser: The decision prompted renewed scrutiny of how platforms handle trademarked keywords.
cards.body:
An Indian court ruling on Google's advertising practices has prompted criticism from tech founders. The decision focuses on how Google handles trademarked keywords in its ad system, with legal experts suggesting it could force platforms to reconsider their approach to trademark-related paid advertising.

The ruling has reignited discussion about search and advertising platforms' management of trademark issues. Founders have seized on the decision to revive broader concerns about Google's ad business practices.

hero.headline: Golden Knights and Hurricanes to meet in Stanley Cup Final
hero.body:
The Vegas Golden Knights will face the Carolina Hurricanes in the Stanley Cup Final, the NHL announced. The series is scheduled to begin either June 2 or June 4.

The Hurricanes advanced to their first Stanley Cup Final in two decades after defeating the Montreal Canadiens 6-1 in Game 5 on Friday night. Carolina had lost three conference finals since 2019 before breaking through this season.

The Golden Knights secured their berth after winning their conference final series. This marks a return to the championship round for Vegas, which has established itself as one of the league's stronger teams since entering the NHL as an expansion franchise.

The exact start date depends on scheduling factors. Game 1 will be played in Carolina, with the Hurricanes hosting the first two games of the series before it shifts to Vegas.

Both teams enter the final seeking the Stanley Cup. The Hurricanes last won the championship in 2006, while the Golden Knights captured their first title in franchise history in 2023. The series represents another opportunity for Vegas to add to its early success and for Carolina to end a long championship drought.

The NHL finalized the schedule after both conference finals concluded. The matchup pairs two teams that demonstrated strong performance throughout the playoffs, setting up what is expected to be a competitive final series.

Carolina's victory over Montreal featured dominant play in the decisive game, allowing the team to close out the series at home. The Hurricanes scored six goals while limiting the Canadiens to one, capping a series in which they won four of five games.

cards.headline: Hurricanes goalie Andersen plays hours after agent's death
cards.teaser: Frederik Andersen took the ice for Carolina in Game 5 against Montreal the day after his agent died by suicide.
cards.body:
Carolina Hurricanes goaltender Frederik Andersen played Friday night in Game 5 against the Montreal Canadiens, just hours after learning of his agent Claude Lemieux's death by suicide.

Despite his grief, Andersen delivered a strong performance as the Hurricanes secured a victory that advanced them to the Stanley Cup Final.

cards.headline: Indiana quarterback bet on Hoosiers games while on team
cards.teaser: Brendan Sorsby placed at least 40 bets involving Indiana football during his time as the team's quarterback.
cards.body:
Former Indiana quarterback Brendan Sorsby placed at least 40 bets on Indiana football while playing for the Hoosiers, according to court documents filed Friday. Over four years, he wagered approximately $90,000 through sportsbook accounts registered to family members and friends.

The betting activity raises potential violations of NCAA rules and regulations that prohibit athletes from wagering on their own teams or sports.

cards.headline: Thunder's Jalen Williams out for Game 7 against Spurs
cards.teaser: Oklahoma City will be without wing Jalen Williams for Saturday's elimination game due to injury.
cards.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder will be without wing Jalen Williams for Saturday's Game 7 against the San Antonio Spurs. Williams, who has battled injuries throughout the season, is unavailable for the decisive playoff contest in Oklahoma City.

The winner of Game 7 will advance to the NBA Finals to face the New York Knicks. The Spurs earned their trip to the deciding game with a dominant 118-91 victory in Game 6, with Victor Wembanyama recording 28 points and 10 rebounds.

cards.headline: Giants receiver Gunner Olszewski suffers potential Achilles injury
cards.teaser: New York fears wide receiver Gunner Olszewski tore his Achilles tendon during Friday's practice.
cards.body:
Giants wide receiver Gunner Olszewski suffered a noncontact injury during organized team activities on Friday that the team fears is a torn Achilles tendon, according to ESPN sources.

A torn Achilles would likely require surgery and sideline Olszewski for an extended period.

cards.headline: Giants teammates express unity after Trump event dispute
cards.teaser: Quarterback Jaxson Dart and linebacker Abdul Carter said they are united following a disagreement over Dart's participation in a presidential event.
cards.body:
New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart and defensive end Abdul Carter expressed solidarity Friday following a disagreement over Dart's participation in an event for President Donald Trump.

The two teammates publicly addressed the situation, emphasizing their unity despite the dispute centered on Dart's involvement with the presidential event.

cards.headline: UCLA's Megan Grant breaks school home run record
cards.teaser: Grant set a new UCLA career home run mark in the Bruins' dominant Women's College World Series victory.
cards.body:
Megan Grant made history at the Women's College World Series, breaking UCLA's career home run record during Friday's matchup against Arkansas. The achievement came during a dominant performance by the Bruins, who dominated the game offensively.

UCLA's lineup was particularly explosive in the second inning, when all nine players in the batting order scored. The Bruins went on to win 11-0, ending the game early under the tournament's run-rule mercy rule.

hero.headline: Marcia Lucas, Oscar-winning Star Wars editor, dies at 80
hero.body:
Marcia Lucas, the Oscar-winning film editor whose work helped shape Star Wars into a cultural phenomenon, died at her home in Rancho Mirage, California. She was 80.

Lucasfilm released a statement expressing deep sadness over her passing. Lucas died following a battle with metastatic cancer.

Lucas was one of three editors to share the Academy Award for editing the original Star Wars film in 1977. Her contributions to the film extended beyond technical craft to shaping its narrative structure and emotional resonance.

Beyond Star Wars, Lucas edited several iconic films of the 1970s, including Martin Scorsese's Taxi Driver. Her editing career placed her at the center of a transformative period in American cinema.

Lucas was formerly married to Star Wars creator George Lucas. The two divorced in the 1980s, but her professional legacy remained distinct and significant in its own right.

Her death represents the loss of a pioneering figure in film editing, an art form that often receives less recognition than directing or acting despite its central role in storytelling. The three editors who shared the Oscar for Star Wars each brought different skills to the project, working together to create the film's distinctive pace and rhythm.

Lucasfilm's tribute acknowledged her contributions to the Star Wars franchise and the broader film industry. Her work on the original film helped establish the template for modern science fiction cinema and demonstrated how editing could transform raw footage into compelling narrative.

Lucas lived in Rancho Mirage, a desert community in Southern California, where she spent her final years. She was 80 years old at the time of her death.

cards.headline: Music executive Clive Davis hospitalized in New York
cards.teaser: The 94-year-old record industry executive was admitted to a New York City hospital for a respiratory issue.
cards.body:
Clive Davis, the music executive who co-founded Bad Boy Records with Sean Combs, was hospitalized in New York City. He was admitted for an upper respiratory infection.

Davis, 94, is expected to recover soon, according to reports. The executive has shaped the careers of numerous artists over his decades-long career in the recording industry.

cards.headline: Frankie Valli cancels remaining 2026 concerts
cards.teaser: The 92-year-old singer announced he is canceling the rest of his scheduled performances this year for health reasons.
cards.body:
Frankie Valli announced Friday that he is canceling his remaining 2026 concert dates to focus on his health. The 92-year-old performer, known for his enduring passion for touring, made the announcement on social media.

Valli expressed his apologies to fans who had purchased tickets to the canceled shows.

cards.headline: Artists drop out of Freedom 250 concert series
cards.teaser: Multiple performers have withdrawn from a concert series marking America's 250th birthday, planned for the National Mall in Washington.
cards.body:
Several artists have withdrawn from the Freedom 250 concert series scheduled for July 6 on the National Mall in Washington, which was organized by the Trump administration to mark America's 250th birthday.

At least seven of the nine featured musical acts dropped out within 48 hours of the lineup being announced. Bret Michaels was among the latest to withdraw, citing a deteriorating atmosphere around the event and threats being made against performers.

cards.headline: Paul McCartney reflects on family during Beatles fame
cards.teaser: The musician described how his family helped him navigate life during the Beatles' rise to international stardom.
cards.body:
Paul McCartney detailed a turning point during the Beatles' rise to fame and how his family grounded him during that period. The musician spoke about navigating life under intense public scrutiny.

McCartney's reflections provide insight into how he managed the pressures of Beatlemania while maintaining connections to his personal life and family relationships.

cards.headline: Nazanin Zaghari-Ratcliffe describes sewing in Iranian prison
cards.teaser: The former prisoner told an audience that creativity provided a psychological escape while her freedom was restricted.
cards.body:
Nazanin Zaghari-Ratcliffe spoke about how sewing served as a lifeline during her imprisonment in Iran. She described the practice as a form of psychological escape.

Speaking to an audience, Zaghari-Ratcliffe said that when freedom is restricted, creativity offers a quick psychological exit. She reflected on her experience using creative outlets to cope with confinement.

cards.headline: Mountain lion tranquilized in Santa Monica neighborhood
cards.teaser: Wildlife officials tracked and removed a mountain lion from a residential area in Santa Monica.
cards.body:
A mountain lion was tranquilized and removed from a residential area in Santa Monica. The sighting put the neighborhood on high alert.

Wildlife officials tracked the animal through the Santa Monica neighborhood before safely capturing it. The incident prompted warnings to residents in the area.

hero.headline: White House releases memo saying Trump in excellent health after physical
hero.body:
President Trump remains in excellent health following his annual medical examination, according to a memo released by the White House on Friday evening.

The president underwent his checkup at Walter Reed National Military Medical Center on Tuesday, where physicians conducted cardiac, neurological, dermatological and other specialized examinations. His doctor's assessment concluded that Trump remains fit to carry out his presidential duties.

The comprehensive evaluation is part of the standard annual medical assessment required for sitting presidents. The examination included multiple specialty evaluations across different areas of health to provide an overall assessment of the president's condition.

However, independent physicians have raised questions about certain findings documented during the physical. These outside medical professionals pointed to recurrent bruises on Trump's hands and swelling in his legs as areas warranting further attention and clarification.

The White House memo released to the public did not address the specific observations raised by independent physicians regarding the bruising and leg swelling. The administration has not provided additional commentary explaining these findings or responding to the concerns voiced by outside medical experts.

Presidents typically release summaries of their medical assessments rather than comprehensive medical records. The release of presidential health information often generates scrutiny from medical professionals outside the administration, who may question findings or seek clarification on particular health observations.

The timing of the memo's release on a Friday evening and the contrast between the official physician's assessment and the questions raised by independent physicians has attracted attention. The White House has not announced any plans to release supplementary details about the president's health status or to specifically address the concerns raised by outside doctors.

The annual physical examination represents one of the formal health evaluations required during a presidency. These assessments serve to provide the public with basic information about the sitting president's medical fitness for office. The official memo stating Trump's excellent health aligns with previous White House statements about the president's condition.

Medical professionals and the public often scrutinize presidential health information closely, particularly when independent observations differ from official assessments. The lack of detailed explanation regarding the bruising and swelling noted by outside physicians may continue to generate questions from medical experts and the media.

The White House's decision to release only a brief memo rather than more comprehensive information about the examination results follows precedent set by previous administrations. However, the gap between the official conclusion of excellent health and the independent physicians' concerns about specific physical findings represents an area where additional transparency could address public questions about the president's medical condition.

cards.headline: Judge allows Trump's $10 billion IRS lawsuit to be reopened
cards.teaser: A federal judge sided with intervenors who said a settlement to create an anti-weaponization fund tainted the case.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Florida agreed to reopen President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS. The decision came after intervenors challenged a previous settlement agreement between the Department of Justice and Trump.

The two sides had agreed to voluntarily dismiss the suit in exchange for creating an anti-weaponization fund. The judge's ruling allows the case to proceed despite that settlement, subjecting it to further legal review.

cards.headline: Trump endorses Pam Evette over Rep. Nancy Mace in South Carolina governor race
cards.teaser: The president backed the lieutenant governor in a primary challenge to the sitting House member.
cards.body:
President Trump endorsed Lt. Gov. Pam Evette in the South Carolina governor's race, backing her over Rep. Nancy Mace. Trump described Evette as an America First Patriot who never wavered.

In a Truth Social post, the president called Evette a good friend, fighter, and winner. The endorsement sets up a primary contest between the sitting lieutenant governor and the sitting House member.

cards.headline: US Southern Command chief meets with Cuban military leaders
cards.teaser: The meeting near Guantanamo Bay occurred amid heightened tensions between the two countries.
cards.body:
The head of U.S. Southern Command met with senior Cuban military leaders on Friday as tensions between the two governments intensify. Commander Gen. Francis L. Donovan spoke with Cuba's First Deputy Minister of the Chief of the General Staff Roberto Legr Sotolongo and other officials near Naval Station Guantanamo Bay.

The meeting came as the Trump administration has stepped up pressure on Cuba. Southern Command announced the session took place amid the broader confrontation between Washington and the island nation.

cards.headline: US military kills three in strike on suspected drug boat in eastern Pacific
cards.teaser: Southern Command said the vessel was transiting along known narco-trafficking routes.
cards.body:
The U.S. military carried out a strike Friday on a boat in the eastern Pacific Ocean, killing three men. U.S. Southern Command said the vessel was engaged in narco-trafficking operations and operated by a designated terrorist organization.

This was the third attack by U.S. forces this week in the region. The strikes are part of a months-long campaign targeting alleged drug boats in the Caribbean Sea and eastern Pacific, with the overall death toll from these operations now exceeding 200 people.

cards.headline: Poll shows Talarico leading Paxton by 3 points in Texas Senate race
cards.teaser: The Democratic state representative had 47 percent support compared to 44 percent for the Republican attorney general.
cards.body:
State Rep. James Talarico holds a narrow lead over Republican Ken Paxton in the Texas Senate race, according to a new poll from Texas Public Opinion Research. Forty-seven percent of likely general election voters backed Talarico compared with 44 percent for Paxton.

The survey was released after Paxton won the Republican primary runoff. Paxton has already begun attacking Talarico, calling him "too low-T for Texas" and making manhood a central theme of the campaign.

cards.headline: Paxton attacks Talarico as 'too low-T for Texas' after primary win
cards.teaser: The Republican Senate nominee put manhood front and center in the race following his runoff victory.
cards.body:
Ken Paxton attacked Democratic nominee James Talarico as "too low-T for Texas" shortly after winning the Republican primary runoff. The remark elevated masculinity as a central campaign theme in the Texas Senate race.

Talarico, a state representative, emerged as Paxton's Democratic opponent. The personal attack signaled that questions about manhood would play a significant role in the general election contest between the two candidates.
